name: Crucible VE-7 'Arc Welder'
description:
A vehicle-mounted directed electromagnetic pulse weapon that discharges a focused EMP cone from an antenna array hidden behind a vehicle's front grille. The VE-7 generates a single-pulse electromagnetic discharge that disables electronic systems in a 30-degree cone extending 50 meters from the vehicle, affecting everything from vehicle engine management computers to personal BCIs to building security systems. The pulse is generated by a capacitor bank that requires 45 seconds to recharge between firings, drawing power from the vehicle's enhanced electrical system.

Crucible developed the VE-7 for convoy escort operations where the primary threat is electronically detonated ambush weapons — IEDs, remote-triggered mines, and drone attacks that rely on electronic command links. The EMP pulse disables the electronic triggers before the convoy reaches the threat area, neutralizing ambushes without requiring the convoy to stop or slow. The weapon's directional focus means it affects only the area ahead of the vehicle, limiting collateral electronic disruption to the vehicle's path.

The VE-7's most concerning application in GLMZ is its effect on BCIs and cyberware. The EMP pulse induces current in any electronic implant within range, causing effects ranging from momentary disorientation to seizures to permanent implant damage depending on the implant's shielding and the subject's distance from the emitter. Using the Arc Welder in a populated area subjects every augmented person in the cone to involuntary neurological disruption. Crucible's safety documentation classifies this as 'incidental electronic interference.' Cyberware manufacturers classify it as assault.
legality: Military — restricted to authorized electronic warfare operations
specifications:
pulse cone: 30 degrees, 50-meter range
effect: Electronic system disruption/destruction
recharge time: 45 seconds
power source: Vehicle electrical system with capacitor bank
collateral: Affects all electronics in cone, including BCIs
weight: 80 kg total system
mounting: Concealed behind front grille
tactical_use: Electronic warfare, convoy protection, and pursuit denial. The Arc Welder disables pursuing vehicles, neutralizes electronic ambushes, and disrupts security systems ahead of the vehicle. Each pulse requires 45 seconds to recharge, making shot selection critical.
cultural_context: The VE-7 is feared by augmented communities more than any ballistic vehicle weapon. A machine gun can miss. An EMP cone affects everything in its path. The knowledge that a passing vehicle might discharge an EMP that fries your neural interface has created a specific paranoia among cyberware users — 'getting arced' is a constant, invisible threat in GLMZ's traffic.
known_users: At least one known criminal operation using EMP for armored car robberies
story_hooks: A VE-7 was discharged on a crowded street, disabling every electronic device in a 50-meter cone — including the BCIs of 30 augmented pedestrians, 4 of whom suffered seizures, 1 of whom died from implant failure. The vehicle was targeting a specific drone overhead. The pedestrians were incidental.

Someone is using a VE-7 to systematically disable security cameras along a specific route through GLMZ, creating an electronic blind corridor that appears to lead from the Shelf to a corporate facility. They're building an invisible path.
related_entities: Tethered Orbital Reconnaissance and Suppression Drone TORSD-7 'Kitestring'

physical_description.visual_profile: A concealed vehicle-mounted weapon system — no visible barrel or traditional gun form. The operational core is a horizontally-arrayed antenna cluster hidden behind the vehicle's front grille, with thick reinforced mounting brackets and a control module barely visible through mesh venting. At rest, completely indistinguishable from standard vehicle infrastructure.
physical_description.dimensions: Antenna array: 120cm width × 45cm height × 35cm depth. Control module: 60cm × 40cm × 30cm. System extends across entire front grille mounting area.
physical_description.weight_description: Substantial and immobile — 80kg total system weight distributed across vehicle frame. The capacitor bank alone creates a noticeable downward bias; designed for permanent installation rather than field repositioning.
physical_description.primary_material: Antenna array: aerospace-grade aluminum alloy with ferrite core elements. Capacitor bank housing: reinforced polymer composite with internal copper winding visible through translucent sections. Control module frame: brushed stainless steel with heat-dissipation fins.
physical_description.finish: Antenna elements: satin silver with anodized aluminum trim. Capacitor housing: matte charcoal polymer with frosted translucent sections revealing copper coil layers beneath. Control module: brushed steel with black powder-coat accent panels. All external surfaces show light oxidation and thermal stress marks.
physical_description.color_scheme: Silver-gray antenna array, charcoal-black housing, stainless steel accents. Status indicator strip in control module glows amber-orange during charging cycle.
physical_description.grip_texture: Not applicable — system is vehicle-mounted and interfaced through vehicle control systems only. Internal heat-sink fins feature knurled grip texture for maintenance access.
distinctive_features: Horizontal antenna array with 7 individual emitter elements spaced precisely 18cm apart
Frosted polymer windows in capacitor bank revealing nested copper windings and dielectric layers
Thermal vent grating across top of control module with micro-fins for heat dissipation
Amber-orange charging indicator strip that cycles intensity during 45-second recharge
Heavy-gauge mounting brackets with vibration dampeners at all connection points
Sealed connector ports with military-spec quick-disconnect couplings
Faint scorch marks and heat discoloration around antenna elements indicating repeated discharge
Maintenance access panel with biometric lock — small handprint scanner flush with surface
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: PureFiber Nutrition corporate logo stamped on control module corner (ironic placement on weapons system). Serial plate mounted on capacitor housing reads: 'CRUCIBLE VE-7 ARC WELDER | MFG 2223 | MILITARY EW ONLY'. Faint factory test markings on antenna mounting brackets.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field-worn but meticulously maintained. Antenna elements show light oxidation from exposure and thermal cycling. Capacitor housing has minor scuff marks from service work. Control module displays signs of heavy use: discolored charge indicator from repeated cycling, reinforced wiring at connector joints suggesting field repairs, thermal stress patterns around vents. Weapon maintains operational readiness despite visible age.
